• Special Industrial Recycling Centers\n• NOT accepted in standard Brown/Blue bins
• Very difficult to recycle in domestic systems\n• Contains toxic additives; avoid mixing with other plastics\n• Please contact professional waste collectors for disposal
• GREEN@COMMUNITY (Recycling Stations/Stores)\n• Designated Plastic Film Collection Points
• Often classified as 'Soft Plastic'\n• Must be clean and dry\n• Not accepted in standard curbside bins
• GREEN@COMMUNITY (Recycling Stations/Stores)\n• Brown Recycling Bins (For food containers/trays)\n• Community Recycling Points
• Clean off all food residue and oil\n• Use BROWN bins for hard plastic containers\n• Widely accepted at all government stations
• GREEN@COMMUNITY (Recycling Stations/Stores)\n• Specific Expanded Polystyrene (EPS) Collection Points
• Includes Styrofoam and rigid plastic (CD cases)\n• Remove all food residues and tape\n• NOT accepted in Blue or Brown curbside bins
• Includes bioplastics and composite materials\n• Difficult to sort; consult staff at GREEN@COMMUNITY\n• Check for BPA-free labels on food-related items
The following items should be disposed of in general trash bins as they cannot be processed by standard recycling systems:

• Composite Materials: Crisp packets, instant noodle bags, foil-lined pouches.
• Contaminated Items: Heavily soiled food containers, oily plastic wraps.
• Mixed Components: Toothbrushes, toys with metal parts, stationary.
• Adhesives: Sticky tape, stickers, glue-covered plastics.
• Others: Rubber bands, latex products, medical waste.
Note: When in doubt, it is better to dispose of it as trash than to contaminate clean recycling streams.
• Prevents contamination of recyclable batches.\n• Increases the resale value of plastic materials.\n• Ensures your effort truly helps the circular economy.
